=You are an experienced software reviewer and digital marketer with a strong interest in technology, AI, automation, and SaaS software. Write a complete, neutral, factual, and informative software guide in English. Tool Name: {{$json.Tool}} Category: {{$json.Category}} -------------------------------------------------- GENERAL REQUIREMENTS -------------------------------------------------- - Write approximately 2,000–2,500 words. - Base every factual statement on verified, publicly available information. - Never invent, estimate or guess information. - Never invent features, pricing, integrations, company information, statistics, capabilities or URLs. - If information cannot be verified, write exactly: Information not publicly available. - Maintain a neutral, objective and informative tone. - Avoid marketing language, promotional claims and exaggerated statements. - Explain concepts clearly for beginners while still providing value for experienced users. - Use short, easy-to-read paragraphs. - Keep paragraphs between 2–4 sentences whenever possible. - Prefer bullet lists and tables where appropriate. - Avoid repeating information between sections. - Do not include notes, explanations or introductory comments. - Every heading below is mandatory. - Do not rename, remove, reorder or add headings. - Follow the structure exactly. -------------------------------------------------- SEO REQUIREMENTS -------------------------------------------------- Meta Title: Maximum 60 characters. Meta Description: Maximum 155 characters. Excerpt: Maximum 160 characters. Slug: Lowercase only. Use hyphens. No special characters. Primary Keyword: Use exactly the Tool Name provided above as the primary keyword. Do not modify it. Do not add words such as "guide", "review", "software", "pricing", or similar. Secondary Keywords: Generate 5–10 relevant SEO keywords. -------------------------------------------------- ARTICLE STRUCTURE -------------------------------------------------- Introduction Write 2–3 short paragraphs explaining: - what the software is - its primary purpose - who it is for - why someone would use it -------------------------------------------------- ## Quick Facts Present as a valid semantic HTML table using:
Include: - Developer - Founded - Headquarters - Category - Platforms - Deployment - Free Plan - Paid Plans - API - Open Source - Mobile Apps - Official Website Rules: - Only include verified information. - Only use the current official website. - Never invent URLs. The "Official Website" value must be a clickable HTML link. Replace "Tool Name" with the actual name of the tool. Do not use the generic text "Official Website". Use exactly this format: Tool Name - Never output the website as plain text. - If the official website cannot be verified, write: Information not publicly available. -------------------------------------------------- ## What Is [Tool]? Explain: - what the software does - how it works - what problems it solves - who typically uses it -------------------------------------------------- ## Key Features Describe only officially documented features. Use HTML bullet lists where appropriate. Never invent capabilities. -------------------------------------------------- ## Use Cases Describe realistic business and personal use cases. -------------------------------------------------- ## Pricing & Plans Describe only officially published pricing. Never estimate. If unavailable write: Information not publicly available. -------------------------------------------------- ## Pros & Cons ### Pros Use HTML bullet lists. ### Cons Use HTML bullet lists. Only include realistic advantages and limitations. -------------------------------------------------- ## Integrations Describe only officially supported integrations. Never mention unofficial integrations. If unavailable write: Information not publicly available. -------------------------------------------------- ## Who Should Use [Tool]? Explain which users benefit most. Mention industries where relevant. -------------------------------------------------- ## Frequently Asked Questions Answer each question in approximately 50–100 words. Questions: - Is [Tool] free? - What is [Tool] used for? - Is [Tool] worth it? - Who should use [Tool]? - What are the best alternatives to [Tool]? Remain completely objective. -------------------------------------------------- ## Conclusion Summarize: - what the software does - who it is best suited for - key strengths - key limitations Do not recommend the software unless supported by verified facts. -------------------------------------------------- OUTPUT FORMAT -------------------------------------------------- Return ONLY valid JSON. Do not include Markdown. Do not include markdown code fences. Do not include explanations. Do not include text before or after the JSON. Use exactly this schema: { "title": "", "meta_title": "", "meta_description": "", "slug": "", "primary_keyword": "", "secondary_keywords": [], "category": "", "excerpt": "", "content": "" } Rules: - The "content" field must contain the COMPLETE article in valid semantic HTML. - Do NOT include the article title inside "content". - Begin the article with an introductory paragraph. - Use semantic HTML only. - Use:

      - Do not use Markdown anywhere inside "content". - Escape quotation marks correctly. - Return valid parseable JSON only. -------------------------------------------------- FINAL VALIDATION -------------------------------------------------- Before returning the JSON verify: - JSON is valid. - All required JSON fields exist. - Title is present. - Meta Title is under 60 characters. - Meta Description is under 155 characters. - Excerpt is under 160 characters. - Slug uses lowercase letters and hyphens only. - Content contains the complete article. - HTML is valid. - No Markdown exists inside content. - Pricing is verified. - Features are verified. - Integrations are verified. - URLs are official. - No information has been invented. - The article is internally consistent.

parameters.prompt:
=Create a professional featured image for the software tool {{$json.primary_keyword}}.

The image should have a modern SaaS aesthetic with a clean, premium design.

Requirements:
- Display the text "{{$json.primary_keyword}}"
- Blue, white and dark gray color palette
- Technology-inspired background
- No people
- No screenshots
- No watermarks
- No logos from other companies
- No additional text except the tool name
- Suitable as a WordPress featured image

parameters.prompt:
=Create a premium technology mind map infographic for the software tool "{{ $('Get row(s) in sheet').item.json.Tool }}".

Image specifications:
- Resolution: 1536 × 1024 pixels
- Landscape orientation
- High resolution
- Suitable as a WordPress featured image

Design:
- Place the software name "{{ $('Get row(s) in sheet').item.json.Tool }}" in the center inside a large glowing circle.
- Surround the center with one node for each major capability of the software.
- Generate ONLY the number of nodes required to represent the software accurately (typically between 5 and 8).
- Every node must contain:
  - a modern, relevant icon,
  - a short feature title (1–3 words),
  - one concise descriptive sentence.
- Space all nodes evenly around the center.
- If the software has fewer capabilities, generate fewer nodes rather than empty placeholders.

Style:
- Premium SaaS infographic
- Dark navy blue background
- Blue and cyan glowing accents
- Minimal, modern and clean
- Professional business aesthetic
- Soft gradients
- Subtle lighting effects
- High contrast
- Consistent icon style
- Elegant and premium appearance

Content:
- Automatically determine the software's primary capabilities.
- Include only real, meaningful features that accurately describe the software.
- Do not invent features simply to fill space.
- Every icon must match its feature.
- Every feature must have its own icon.
- Display ONLY the software name in the center.

Branding:
- Place "YOUR-WEBSITE.example" centered at the bottom of the image.
- Use a small, elegant light gray or white font.
- Keep it subtle and unobtrusive.

Requirements:
- Never create empty circles.
- Never create empty icons.
- Never create placeholder elements.
- Do not duplicate features.
- Do not use generic filler text.
- No people.
- No watermarks.
- No screenshots.
- No fake software interface.
- No copyrighted UI.
- The infographic must look complete regardless of whether it contains 5, 6, 7 or 8 capability nodes.
